critique.feedback: The grouping, filters, and relationship path are all correct: the query returns one row per country (Cypher implicitly groups by the non-aggregated c.name), keeps only people with confirmedtime before 2020-04-15, and follows the only schema-supported path (Person)-[:PERFORMS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:LOCATED_AT]->(:Place)-[:PART_OF]->(:Region)-[:PART_OF]->(:Country). The problem is the duration aggregation. Schema shows Visit.duration has type DURATION, and the question asks for the average duration in SECONDS. In Neo4j, toFloat() only accepts INTEGER, FLOAT, or STRING and does not convert a DURATION; the query will therefore throw a type error at runtime, and even if it ran, the raw duration would not be in seconds. Replace avg(toFloat(v.duration)) with avg(duration.inSeconds(v.duration)), which converts each Visit.duration to a whole number of seconds and then averages them per country. Keep count(v) as the total visit count; do not switch to AVG(DISTINCT ...), since that would drop legitimate visits that happen to share the same duration.
